atlas-au.0081: The Australian Government Graduate Program requires Australian citizenship, takes graduates with a degree completed in a set recent window, and opens applications on 1 March 2027 for the next intake (programmes typically start around February); the first stage takes about six weeks, then candidates enter a merit pool and are matched to agencies.
atlas-au.0082: The Australian Signals Directorate runs a 12-month graduate programme with three rotations, for citizens with a degree finished in the past 5 years, starting salary A$83,489; its 2027 round closed on 6 April 2026.
atlas-au.0084: GradConnection (now SEEK Grad) lists graduate programmes, internships, cadetships and clerkships for employers; its homepage showed 864 graduate and internship programmes on the day it was read.
atlas-au.0085: Universities run career fairs and expos: the University of Sydney’s graduate job and internship fair was held on 5 March 2026 for employers and students and alumni from all disciplines.
atlas-au.0087: Experienced hires apply directly on employer career pages and through recruiters; Michael Page lists a graduate programme and accounting, finance and technology recruiting across offices in Brisbane, Canberra, Melbourne, Perth and Sydney.
atlas-au.0088: Because applications per employer are rising, a plain cold application competes with many structured entries; keep the pay bands and rolling intakes in view.
atlas-au.0090: Online applications, tests and assessment centres for graduate programmes; networking matters more at smaller firms.
atlas-au.0091: Many graduate programmes are restricted to citizens and permanent residents; 22.8% of postgraduates in jobs below their level named the lack of permanent residency as the reason.
atlas-au.0092: The market is crowded rather than closed: employers kept the number of graduate roles stable at an average of 52 while graduate applications per employer rose 23%, and the share of international undergraduates in full-time work was 50.8% in 2025 against 75.4% of domestic ones.
atlas-au.0093: The 2025 survey changed how the labour force is defined, so the 2025 full-time rates are not directly comparable with earlier years.
atlas-au.0094: The big banks run graduate programmes starting each February, with applications from about March of the year before: Commonwealth Bank’s 2026 banking and accounting programme paid A$75,000 to 95,000; Macquarie’s 12-to-24-month programme starts in Sydney.
atlas-au.0095: Macquarie’s round for a February 2027 start ran later, from 21 September to 13 October 2026, so the window differs by firm.
atlas-au.0096: The Big Four are the largest graduate employers: in 2022 they took nearly 4,700 of the 6,200 graduates hired by the 100 largest accounting firms. With an expected shortfall of 6,000 accountants by 2030, they now also recruit non-accounting graduates with AI skills and train them.
atlas-au.0097: KPMG’s 2027 audit programme has a main intake that has closed and a rolling intake reviewed as roles open; it starts around February 2027.
atlas-au.0098: The APS had 198,529 employees at 30 June 2025, 70,221 of them in the Australian Capital Territory. Its graduate programme requires citizenship, as does the Australian Signals Directorate.
atlas-au.0099: Atlassian and Canva run graduate software programmes in Sydney, but Atlassian’s takes only Australian and New Zealand citizens, permanent residents and student-visa holders and does not sponsor visas.
atlas-au.0100: ASD’s graduate programme has a Cyber stream beside Analyst and Technologist; most positions are in Canberra, with offices in Brisbane, Melbourne and Perth, and it requires a Positive Vetting security clearance.
atlas-au.0101: The pages read set eligibility by study status and results, not by school: Macquarie takes final-year students from all degree backgrounds, and ASD asks for a bachelor’s degree with a minimum credit average. Universities still host the fairs and boards through which employers reach students.
atlas-au.0102: Universities host graduate job and internship fairs in the first term (Sydney’s was on 5 March 2026), and the Australian Association of Graduate Employers holds its annual graduate recruitment and development conference on 11 and 12 November 2026 in Sydney.
atlas-au.0103: Programme rounds cluster in the year before the February start: Macquarie’s graduate round ran 21 September to 13 October 2026 and its summer internship closed in July and August; the federal programme opens on 1 March 2027; KPMG keeps a rolling intake after its main one.
atlas-au.0104: The pages read ask for a bachelor’s degree, not a master’s: ASD requires a bachelor’s degree completed in the past 5 years, and Macquarie takes final-year students from all degree backgrounds. International business and management postgraduate coursework graduates were in full-time work at 53.3% against 92.2% for domestic ones.
atlas-au.0105: For regulated occupations the Department of Education sends you to the registration, licensing or professional body; for jobs with no specific qualification requirement, citizens and permanent residents can ask a state or territory Overseas Qualifications Unit to compare a foreign degree, and commercial assessment services also exist.
atlas-au.0106: The programme pages read name no target schools: Macquarie accepts all degree backgrounds and ASD sets a minimum credit average, so results and fit count more than the university name.
atlas-au.0107: Cadetship and apprenticeship programmes exist beside graduate programmes: ASD runs a 2027 apprenticeship programme and a 2027 cadetship programme, and GradConnection lists cadetships and clerkships; they are a side door, not the main route.
atlas-au.0108: The APS had 198,529 employees at 30 June 2025, including 184,442 ongoing, with Services Australia (35,210), the Australian Taxation Office (21,436) and Defence (20,545) the largest; 70,221 were in the Australian Capital Territory.
atlas-au.0109: Graduate programmes rarely sponsor: Atlassian does not sponsor visas, the federal and ASD programmes need citizenship, and the Core Skills stream of the 482 visa asks for at least one year of relevant experience and pay of at least A$79,499. See Visas for the rules.
atlas-au.0110: No photo or date of birth: UNSW’s guide says not to include a photograph, date of birth, gender or marital status.
atlas-au.0111: Resumes are commonly 2 pages, and some employers ask for 1; a GradConnection guide aims for one page with limited experience and two at most, and UNSW allows 3 pages only for people with extensive experience or research output.
atlas-au.0112: KPMG’s 2027 programme starts with a five-minute application form rather than a letter; public-service applications, by contrast, are tailored to the selection criteria. A letter is added when the posting asks for one.
atlas-au.0113: The referees section ends the resume and can be names, “available on request” or left to later; UNSW notes one international referee is acceptable if a local one is also given, and GradConnection says references need not appear unless the employer states it. Ask permission first.
atlas-au.0114: For the federal programme, applicants prepare personal details, work and education history, an academic transcript and proof of citizenship; the application is made online.
atlas-au.0115: Graduate programmes show a pay band rather than asking for a figure: KPMG lists A$60,000 to 80,000 and ASD A$83,489; salary expectations are an issue for experienced hires, not for the application form.
atlas-au.0116: Checks are routine and run with consent: the National Police Checking Service can run a check only with the applicant’s informed consent for that purpose, and the federal programme requires willingness to undergo police, character and health checks.
atlas-au.0117: ASD goes further: a Positive Vetting security clearance and an Organisational Suitability Assessment for the preferred applicant.
atlas-au.0118: Graduate programmes rarely sponsor visas; a temporary graduate visa after an Australian degree is the usual way to be eligible.
atlas-au.0119: Some graduate programmes do take international applicants: KPMG’s listing says it accepts them, though the work-rights list was cut off on the page read.
atlas-au.0120: English. A Core Skills 482 application asks for English at IELTS 5.0 overall or an equivalent; graduate programmes state no further language requirement on the pages read.
atlas-au.0121: Typical graduate selection starts with a short form, then online assessments, then interviews or an assessment centre: KPMG’s 2027 listing describes a five-minute form followed by online assessments, and the federal programme takes about six weeks for its first stage before a merit pool and matching.
atlas-au.0122: Candidates use AI: 42% used an AI tool during recruitment in 2026 (27% in 2025), 70% use it for interview preparation, and 1 in 4 keep applying after accepting an offer.
atlas-au.0123: Security-cleared employers add vetting: ASD requires a Positive Vetting clearance for the whole employment and an Organisational Suitability Assessment for the preferred applicant.
atlas-au.0124: Offers for the main round are timed to the February start: Macquarie’s graduate programme starts in February 2027 after a September–October round, and graduates keep options open (multiple-offer acceptance rose from 9% in 2024 to 17% in 2025).
atlas-au.0125: Notice under the National Employment Standards is 1 week up to 1 year of service, 2 weeks up to 3 years, 3 weeks up to 5 years and 4 weeks beyond; probation does not remove the entitlement, and fixed-term and casual staff are excluded.
atlas-au.0126: Unfair-dismissal protection needs at least 6 months with the employer, or 12 months in a small business; graduate pay is set by the programme band rather than negotiated.
atlas-au.0127: Few graduate employers sponsor, so ask before you invest: Atlassian does not sponsor visas, the federal and ASD programmes need citizenship, and KPMG says it accepts international applicants without a readable work-rights list.
